subject: MAP: pilot cost sensitivity, eval gating & procurement summary

Subject: MAP: pilot cost sensitivity, eval gating & procurement summary

Samir / Aisha,

Great talk today 5. Per our agreement I attached a concise sensitivity workbook (HL-Pilot-Cost-Sensitivity-v1.xlsx) and a procurement-friendly one-pager. I want to make the MAP gating explicit around the unit economics so procurement can run the ERP scenarios quickly. Key assumptions in the attached workbook (tab: summary):

- Pricing lines: hosted generation = $0.00080/token; hosted embeddings = $0.000006/token. We also show an illustrative dedicated commit price (25% off gen) for comparison.
- Workload split: we used two workload classes for pilot planning: triage (short, high-QPS) and summarization (long, low-QPS).
- Cache modeling: triage template reuse gives higher fraction of prefix caching; default sheet uses 40% triage cache hit, 5% summary cache hit.
- Batching & latency: example run uses concurrency=12 and a 20ms batching window leading to ~18-25% throughput improvement depending on request size. We call out P95 latency impacts separately for hosted vs dedicated.
- Eval gating: recommended 3-week run with 100k tokens/week (300k total) and three prompt sets (functional smoke, edge-case, fairness). MAP item: if evals exceed 5% degradation vs baseline on prioritized prompts, automatic rollback and credit mechanics apply.

Can you confirm the following so I can finalize the MAP: which pricing line you prefer to present to procurement (hosted only vs hosted+dedi), expected monthly pilot request volume (order of magnitude), and whether your security team needs additional artifact links?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales 5 East, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HL-Pilot-Cost-Sensitivity-v1.xlsx (workbook), procurement_onepager.pdf (one-page summary)

Thanks Neha 5 this is helpful. A few follow-ups from product and finance: 

- Token rate question: is the $0.00080/token for non-streamed (complete) responses or is this the per-token streaming rate? Our summarization workload has avg context ~3k tokens and we want to understand any non-linear pricing or long-context uplift.
- Cache split: agree triage will have higher reuse; can you provide the sensitivity table with triage cache at 20%, 40%, and 60% and summary cache at 0%, 2.5%, and 5%? Procurement wants a low/med/high scenario.
- Latency SLOs: we need explicit P50/P95 numbers per scenario. For triage, product expects P95 < 400ms. If batching increases P95 > 400ms, we need an alternate config for triage traffic.

I'll get procurement in the thread once we have the low/med/high sensitivity and the per-scenario P95 numbers.

Samir
VP Product, HealthLytics

Adding concrete numbers and a three-scenario sensitivity here (pasted from our internal calc):

- Base pricing used: hosted gen = $0.00080/token; embed = $0.000006/token. Dedicated illustrative = hosted * 0.75 for gen.
- Pilot footprint assumption (example): 200k requests/month total. Workload split triage=70% (avg billed tokens/request 60), summary=30% (avg billed tokens/request 2,400).

Low / Mid / High scenarios (billed tokens & spend):
- Low (higher caching): triage cache 60%, summary cache 0% -> billed tokens ~7.1M -> spend hosted ~$5,680/month.
- Mid (default): triage cache 40%, summary cache 5% -> billed tokens ~18.7M -> spend hosted ~$14,960/month.
- High (low caching, longer contexts): triage cache 20%, summary cache 0% -> billed tokens ~28.4M -> spend hosted~$22,720/month.

Batching/latency callouts:
- With our default hosted batching window and concurrency=12: triage P95 ~420ms (short requests), dedicated tuned profile P95 ~330ms.
- If triage needs strict P95 < 400ms we recommend pinning triage traffic to a lower-batching route or dedicated pool in the MAP.

Eval gating: recommend 100k tokens/week for 3 weeks (300k total) and a canary rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over three weeks. If regression >5% on prioritized prompts, MAP triggers rollback + credit for affected traffic-days.

5Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Aisha / Samir,

Attached is the procurement one-pager (procurement_onepager.pdf) plus the workbook with the single-line table on tab "procurement_summary". Quick highlights to paste into PO worksheet:

- Low (hosted): 7.1M billed tokens -> $5,680/month. Dedicated illustrative -> $4,260/month (25% off).
- Mid (hosted): 18.7M billed tokens -> $14,960/month. Dedicated illustrative -> $11,220/month.
- High (hosted): 28.4M billed tokens -> $22,720/month. Dedicated illustrative -> $17,040/month.
- Eval gating: 300k tokens total (100k/week for 3 weeks).
- Rollback credit formula: prorated_credit = (affected_billed_tokens / days_in_billing_period) * daily_rate * percent_traffic_affected; MAP includes automatic rollback to verified model for traffic >80% until issue addressed.

Next steps: I will upload both files to the shared Drive and send a DocuSign SOW link to procurement. If we receive PO by Oct 8, target kickoff Oct 15 with a 3-week eval and staged ramp to production by Nov 8.

-Neha
Head of Sales 5 East, Redwood Inference
